authority: Polia AI System Architecture / Jewish Knowledge Layer
description: Comprehensive hierarchical taxonomy of Judaism covering identity, history, canon, textual traditions, halakha, theology, worship, intellectual streams, interfaith, and apologetics.

branches.title: Identity, Terminology, and Peoplehood
branches.description: Rigorous linguistic, ethnic, religious, and legal definitions distinguishing Jewish identity categories.

categories.definition: The monotheistic religious, ethical, and cultural system of the Jewish people founded upon the covenant and Torah.

Member of the Jewish people, historically derived from the tribe/kingdom of Judah (Yehudah); defined halakhically by matrilineal descent or formal conversion, though definitions vary across modern denominations.
Descendant of Jacob/Israel; members of the twelve tribes in the biblical and Second Temple periods.
Ancient ethnonym associated with Abraham (the one from beyond the river) and the Northwest Semitic language.
Qur'anic and Islamic designation for the Children of Israel, recipients of the prophetic lineage and divine covenant.
Ethno-cultural divisions including Ashkenazim, Sephardim, Mizrahim, Teimanim, and Beta Israel.
Transnational collective consciousness and existential solidarity binding Jews across historical eras and geographical boundaries.

branches.title: Chronological Jewish History
branches.description: Historiographical periods from Bronze Age origins to contemporary global Jewry.

milestones: Northern Kingdom of Israel (fell 722 BCE to Assyria)
Destruction of Temple 70 CE by Titus
Birth of Reform, Orthodox, Conservative movements
Systematic Nazi murder of 6 million European Jews

branches.title: Tanakh (Hebrew Bible) & Canon
branches.description: Tripartite canon (Torah, Nevi'im, Ketuvim), 24 books, textual witnesses, and contrast with Christian Old Testament.

categories.name: Tanakh vs Christian Old Testament
categories.description: Distinct canonical count (24 books vs 39/46/49), distinct arrangement (Ketuvim ending with Chronicles vs Malachi), and differing theological teleology.

branches.title: Textual Traditions and Languages
branches.description: Manuscripts, critical editions, vocalization traditions, and Semitic philology.

categories.name: Septuagint (LXX)
significance: Textual divergences reflecting alternative Hebrew Vorlage

branches.title: Halakha, Mitzvot, and Rabbinic Law
branches.description: Legal frameworks, commandment enumerations, oral traditions, and jurisprudential methodology.

categories.name: Dual Torah Doctrine
categories.description: Written Torah (Tanakh) and Oral Torah (Mishnah, Gemara, Halakhic codes) received at Sinai.

categories.name: 613 Commandments (Taryag Mitzvot)
categories.breakdown: 248 positive commandments (mitzvot aseh), 365 negative commandments (mitzvot lo ta'aseh)

categories.name: Dietary Laws (Kashrut)
concepts: Prohibition of meat and milk (basar be-chalav)

categories.name: Taharah and Tum'ah (Purity & Impurity)
concepts: Historical Temple purity vs post-Temple rabbinic application

categories.name: Mishpat Ivri (Civil and Family Law)
concepts: Dina de-malkhuta dina (the law of the land is the law)

branches.title: Jewish Theology and Dogmatics
branches.description: Ontological, eschatological, and existential convictions across rabbinic and philosophical traditions.

categories.name: Pure Monotheism & Divine Incorporeality
concepts: Rejection of polytheism, dualism, and trinitarianism

categories.name: Sin, Teshuvah, and Atonement
concepts: Yetzer Ha-Tov and Yetzer Ha-Ra (dual human impulses)
Teshuvah (repentance through confession, regret, cessation, restitution)
Atonement via prayer, charity, suffering, and Yom Kippur independent of animal sacrifice

categories.name: Mashiach (Messiah) & Messianic Era
criteria: Mortal human king from Davidic patrilineal descent
Gathering of exiles to Land of Israel
Restoration of Temple and Torah observance
Universal knowledge of God and global peace (Isa 2, 11; Mic 4)

categories.name: Olam Ha-Ba & Techiyat Ha-Metim
concepts: Gehinnom (temporary purgative purification, not eternal damnation)

categories.name: Shekhinah & Divine Immanence
categories.description: The indwelling divine presence dwelling among Israel, in exile, and in sacred study.

branches.title: Worship, Liturgy, Festivals, and Lifecycle
branches.description: Liturgy, sacred calendar, rites of passage, and communal institutions.

categories.name: Shalosh Regalim (Three Pilgrimage Festivals)
festivals: Shavuot (Feast of Weeks, Sinai revelation, Book of Ruth)
Sukkot (Booths, wilderness wanderings, Lulav and Etrog)

categories.name: Yamim Nora'im (Days of Awe)
festivals: Rosh Hashanah (New Year, Shofar, Day of Judgment)
Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement, 25-hour fast, confession)

categories.name: Post-Biblical Rabbinic Festivals
festivals: Purim (Deliverance from Haman, Megillat Esther, Mishloach Manot)
Tisha B'Av (Fast of the Ninth of Av mourning Temple destructions)

categories.name: Lifecycle Observances
rites: Taharah, Keriah, Shiva, Shloshim, Kaddish Yatom (mourning)

branches.title: Denominations, Movements, and Sub-Traditions
branches.description: Historical sects and modern denominational architectures with distinct halakhic methodologies.

features: Primacy of Torah study (Yeshiva world, Kollel)
Halakhic commitment combined with active engagement with secular education, science, and modern society
Halakha is binding but evolves dynamically over time
Committee on Jewish Law and Standards (CJLS)
Primacy of ethical monotheism over ritual law
Judaism as an evolving religious civilization
The people produce the religion rather than vice versa
Rejection of the Oral Torah and Rabbinic authority
Historical flowering in Islamic Middle East (8th–12th c.)
Identification through Jewish heritage, literature, ethics, history, and peoplehood without religious dogma or ritual practice

branches.title: Comparative Religion and Interfaith Relations
branches.description: Theological, textual, and historical relations between Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

analysis: Jesus as first-century Galilean Jew operating within Second Temple Jewish matrix
Disputes with scribes/Pharisees on halakhic stringencies
Rejection of Jesus as Messiah due to unfulfilled prophetic criteria (world peace, ingathering, Temple)
Rejection of divine sonship and incarnation as incompatible with monotheism
Parting of the ways (1st–4th c. CE)
Pauline repudiation of Mosaic law for Gentiles
Trinitarian dogma vs absolute divine simplicity
Supersessionism / Replacement Theology vs Jewish covenantal continuity
Disputed proof-texts: Isaiah 7:14 ('almah), Isaiah 53 (Suffering Servant), Psalm 22, Psalm 110
Prophets common to both (Ibrahim, Musa, Dawud, Sulayman)
Pact of Umar and Dhimmi status under Islamic rule
Judeo-Arabic literary and philosophical flowering (Saadia, Maimonides, Judah Halevi)
Tahrif al-Ma'na (corruption of interpretation / misrepresentation of meaning)
Classical exegetes: Tabari, Razi, Ibn Hazm, Ibn Taymiyyah
Academic manuscript evidence and Jewish textual preservation

branches.title: Jewish Apologetics, Polemics, and Debate Structures
branches.description: Classical and modern defense of Jewish tradition against external theological challenges.

works: Hizzuk Emunah / Faith Strengthened (Isaac of Troki 1593)

arguments: Permanence and unalterability of Mosaic Torah (Deut 13, Malachi 3:22)
National public revelation at Sinai as epistemic bedrock
Literal vs allegorical reading of messianic peace prophecies
Non-vicarious personal responsibility for sin (Deut 24:16, Ezek 18:20)

categories.theme: Separation of Judaism, Israel, and Zionism
principles: Judaism is a 3,000+ year-old religion and covenant
Zionism is a late 19th-century political movement
State of Israel is a modern geopolitical nation-state founded in 1948
Not all Jews are Israeli; not all Israelis are Jewish; not all religious Jews are Zionists
